clue.text: Radical Aussie in the main fully backs islands

indicators.note: the whole assembled string turns round, read from its end back to its start
the radical and the Aussie sit inside the sea

parts.note: the main is an old poetic name for the sea
R is a standard abbreviation for radical
Oz is slang for Australia, standing for an Aussie

explanation.surface: A wild Australian out at sea keeps backing some islands.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the main' is the old poetic term for the ocean. 'fully backs' reverses the whole build, SEROZA, not just one piece.
explanation.definitionFit: The Azores are a Portuguese archipelago in the mid-Atlantic, so the plural noun fits.

clue.text: Eden's nemesis lifted Olympian

indicators.note: in a down clue, lifted means the word is turned upside down, read from bottom to top

parts.note: Anthony Eden resigned as British prime minister after the 1956 Suez Crisis

explanation.surface: Something that ruined Eden carried off a god from Mount Olympus.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Eden' looks like the Garden of Eden, but it is the British prime minister brought down by the Suez Crisis.
explanation.definitionFit: Zeus was king of the gods who lived on Mount Olympus, the chief Olympian.

clue.text: Alpine factory bears shock

indicators.note: in a down clue the factory bears the shock on top of it, so it comes second

parts.note: a shock or jolt can rock you, so rock is used here
a plant is a factory or works

explanation.surface: A factory in the Alps takes a nasty jolt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Alpine' reads as an adjective for the factory, but it is the definition: a noun for a mountain plant.
explanation.definitionFit: An alpine is a small plant from high mountains, the kind grown in rock gardens.

clue.text: Both burden and support for rider

definitions.meaning: the seat a horse rider sits on

explanation.surface: Something that both weighs on a rider and holds them up.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb sense means to load someone with a task; the noun is the seat strapped to a horse.

clue.text: Hard rock outside broadcast with two chaps

parts.note: Sid and Ian are two men's names, side by side

explanation.surface: A heavy metal band's gig is broadcast live with two blokes presenting.
explanation.definitionFit: Obsidian is a hard, glassy volcanic stone.

clue.text: Where 11 is happiest

definitions.meaning: 11 is POLE POSITION; a pole, North or South, sits at the top or bottom of the globe
to be ... is to be elated

explanation.surface: Where the pole position sits is the happiest place.
explanation.walkthrough: The cross-reference reads 11 as its answer; the pole half of it is at the top of the globe.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom for being elated, and literally where the North Pole is on a globe.

clue.text: Burns for one ugly mascot in tin

indicators.note: the shuffled letters go inside the symbol for tin

parts.note: Sn is the chemical symbol for tin

indicators.note: something ugly is misshapen, so the letters are reshaped

explanation.surface: A football club's mascot blazes away inside a tin can.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Burns' looks like a verb about fire; it is the poet Robert Burns. 'ugly' makes COTSMA from MASCOT, which goes 'in' SN.
explanation.definitionFit: Robert Burns was Scotland's national poet, an example of a man from Scotland.

clue.text: Dutch left broken pottery they produced

indicators.note: broken means the letters are smashed and put together in a new order

explanation.surface: The Dutch abandoned the broken crockery they had made.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broken' rearranges the word left to give ELFT. 'they' refers back to the Dutch, so most of the clue doubles as definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Delft is the blue-and-white tin-glazed earthenware made in the Dutch town of that name.

clue.text: Translate a long special transmitter's crude language

indicators.note: to translate is to convert into another form, so the letters are converted into a new order

parts.note: an axon is the nerve fibre that transmits impulses away from a nerve cell

explanation.surface: Turn a lengthy special radio broadcast into rude words.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Translate' rearranges A LONG into ANGLO. 'transmitter' sounds like radio but is the nerve fibre.
explanation.definitionFit: Anglo-Saxon words are the blunt, earthy vocabulary of English, so the phrase is used for swearing.

clue.text: Wine and grape juice impressing old rebel

indicators.note: to impress is to press in, so the rebel is pressed into the juice

parts.note: must is unfermented grape juice
Jack Cade led a rebellion in Kent in 1450

explanation.surface: A wine and grape juice win over an old revolutionary.
explanation.walkthrough: 'impressing' looks like winning someone over; it means pressing one thing inside another.
explanation.definitionFit: Muscadet is a dry white wine from the Loire valley.

clue.text: Round on major European controlling large force

parts.note: O is round in shape

indicators.note: what controls something holds it within its grip, so these letters enclose the other

parts.note: big and major both mean large or important
L is the abbreviation for large, as on clothing

explanation.surface: A senior European commander turns on a large army under his control.
explanation.definitionFit: To oblige someone is to compel them, as in being obliged to pay.

clue.text: Scott fell short of this perfect spot for Hamilton

definitions.meaning: Captain Scott reached the South Pole only after Amundsen, so failed to take the pole first
the front of the starting grid in Formula One, where Lewis Hamilton races

explanation.surface: An explorer missed out on what a racing driver craves.
explanation.walkthrough: Scott is Robert Falcon Scott of Antarctica; Hamilton is the Formula One driver.
explanation.definitionFit: The front slot on a race grid, and punningly the position of being first at the Pole.

clue.text: State clubs provided last of Ohio sailors inter alia

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for clubs in card games

indicators.note: inter means to place among, so the pieces are set into the Latin word

parts.note: if means provided that

indicators.note: takes the final letter of the word Ohio

parts.note: RN is the Royal Navy, i.e. sailors

explanation.surface: A state's clubs supplied Ohio's last sailors, among other things.
explanation.walkthrough: 'inter alia' looks like the Latin 'among other things', but 'inter' puts IF, O and RN into ALIA.
explanation.definitionFit: California is a US state on the Pacific coast.

clue.text: Strip 1's top couple entering Georgia

indicators.note: the two letters go into the abbreviation for Georgia

parts.note: GA is the postal abbreviation for the US state of Georgia

indicators.note: keeping only the top couple of letters of the answer to 1 across means dropping the rest

parts.note: a number in a clue refers to another entry's answer; this is the answer to 1 across, the Atlantic islands

explanation.surface: The leading pair from the islands move into a strip of Georgia.
explanation.walkthrough: '1' points to the answer to 1 across; 'top couple' keeps its first two letters, so ORES is dropped.
explanation.definitionFit: The Gaza Strip is the coastal territory on the Mediterranean bordering Egypt and Israel.

clue.text: Meat in fine French drink for Chesterton's criminal

indicators.note: the meat goes inside the other two pieces

parts.note: F is the pencil-grade abbreviation for fine
eau is French for water
lamb is a meat

explanation.surface: A criminal tucks into meat with a fine French drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Flambeau is the master thief who becomes Father Brown's ally in G K Chesterton's stories.

clue.text: Carry round energy drink and lots of cold water

indicators.note: the carrying word goes round the energy symbol

parts.note: to bring is to carry something along
E is the physics symbol for energy
the drink is slang for the sea

explanation.surface: Fetch an energy drink and plenty of cold water.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drink' looks like a can of pop, but 'the drink' is slang for the sea.
explanation.definitionFit: The Bering Sea is the cold northern Pacific between Alaska and Siberia.

clue.text: A 6 raised supporters inside state

indicators.note: the supporters go inside the reversed name
in a down clue, raised means read from the bottom up

parts.note: 6 down is SCOTSMAN; Ken is a typical Scotsman's name
bras are supporting underwear

explanation.surface: A raised Scotsman with supporters inside a state.
explanation.walkthrough: 'raised' turns KEN into NEK, which holds BRAS; A comes last.
explanation.definitionFit: Nebraska is a Great Plains state of the US.

clue.text: Thief stupidly cases two papers for tiny part

indicators.note: to case is to enclose, so the jumbled letters wrap the papers
done stupidly means done chaotically, so the letters come out jumbled

parts.note: FT is the Financial Times and i is a British newspaper

explanation.surface: A dim thief breaks into a pair of newspapers' offices for a pittance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stupidly' makes FIETH from THIEF, and 'cases' wraps it round FT and I.
explanation.definitionFit: A fiftieth share is a small fraction of the whole.

clue.text: Cross staff holding ring

indicators.note: the staff holds the ring within it

parts.note: a rod is a staff or stick
O is ring-shaped

explanation.surface: An angry staff member holds a ring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cross' looks like 'angry', but it is a noun.
explanation.definitionFit: A rood is a crucifix, especially a large one above a church screen.

clue.text: Ordinary bloke's guarding island for some Arabs

indicators.note: to guard is to surround protectively, so the island sits within

parts.note: a bloke is a man, and the 's adds S

explanation.surface: An ordinary man protects an island on behalf of some Arabs.
explanation.definitionFit: Omanis are people from Oman, an Arab nation.

clue.text: Noble state of 19 covers tracks with rural resident

indicators.note: in an across entry the state comes after and closes off the preceding pieces

parts.note: a count is a nobleman
RY is the abbreviation for railway
19 down is OMANIS, people of Oman

explanation.surface: A nobleman from an Arab state covers his tracks among country folk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'covers tracks' reads as hiding one's traces, but 'covers' only places the state after the railway and 'with' pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A countrywoman is a woman who lives in the countryside.

clue.text: Wanting marshal to capture east Germany

indicators.note: the marshal captures the two letters, holding them inside

parts.note: Michel Ney was one of Napoleon's marshals
D is the international vehicle code for Germany

explanation.surface: A field marshal is keen to seize East Germany.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wanting' looks like desire, but it means lacking.
explanation.definitionFit: The needy are those wanting, i.e. lacking, the basics.

clue.text: Entrance a duke with vermouth

parts.note: It is short for Italian vermouth, as in gin and it

explanation.surface: A duke makes his entrance with a glass of vermouth.
explanation.definitionFit: An adit is a horizontal passage into a mine.

clue.text: Leaderless team infuriates French city

indicators.note: having no leader means the team name loses its first letter

parts.note: Rangers is a Glasgow football team

explanation.surface: A team without a captain enrages a French city.
explanation.walkthrough: Rangers is a Glasgow football club. Three readings meet here: the trimmed team, the verb and the city.
explanation.definitionFit: To anger is to infuriate; Angers is also a city on the Loire in western France.

clue.text: Call squad to get best place to watch contest

parts.note: to ring is to call on the phone
a side is a team or squad

explanation.surface: Phone the team to get the best seats for the fight.
explanation.definitionFit: A ringside seat is next to the boxing ring, the closest view of a bout.

clue.text: State allowed to settle without Republican

indicators.note: without in its old sense means outside, so these letters go outside the Republican

parts.note: may means is allowed to
to land is to come down and settle

explanation.surface: A state let settlers in but kept Republicans out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' seems to mean lacking, but here it is the old sense 'outside', wrapping MAYLAND round R.
explanation.definitionFit: Maryland is a US state on the Atlantic coast.

clue.text: Old city state's role in South America

indicators.note: the role goes inside the abbreviation

parts.note: a part is a role in a play

explanation.surface: An ancient state plays a role in South America.
explanation.definitionFit: Sparta was an ancient Greek city-state famed for its warriors.
